packages.label: כָּבוֹד וּמַלְכוּת
packages.reason: The largest connected component in Torah #67 centers on כָּבוֹד (divine honor/glory) as the essential nature shared by מַלְכוּת (kingship), כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת (the crown of kingship), and שֻׁלְחָנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם (the person's table). These are all parallel expressions of the same royal/holy domain: the table is the crown of kingship (Yoma 72b), and the crown of kingship is the honor, and the honor is kingship (מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד, Psalm 24:7). Also in this component: כָּבוֹד is the bechina of אֵשׁ (fire, 'וּכְבוֹד ה׳ כְּאֵשׁ אֹכֶלֶת'), of קֹדֶשׁ (holiness, 'וְנִקְדַּשׁ בִּכְבוֹדִי'), and of חַוָּה (the mother of all life, since kavod is the root/source of all souls). The שֻׁלְחָן שֶׁבִּקְדֻשָּׁה (the table in holiness) is the bechina of מַלְכוּת from the side of מַלְכוּת itself, completing the ring. All these concepts share the single essential nature: the sacred presence of divine kingship as an anchoring, life-giving reality. Four 2-node pairs are merged here: (a) נֶפֶשׁ↔לֵּב — the heart/soul pair belongs in the kavod-kingship cluster because the Torah's entire argument is that the נֶפֶשׁ dwells within the כָּבוֹד, and when the heart distances itself from prayer the נֶפֶשׁ distances from כָּבוֹד — their essential bechina is that both are the 'inner life' that connects to כָּבוֹד; (b) שְׁמוּעָה טוֹבָה↔קוֹל הָרְעָמִים — thunder is the voice of divine honor ('אֵל הַכָּבוֹד הִרְעִים', Psalm 29:3), good tidings are the sound of thunder when the Rebbe reveals wisdom; these belong in the kavod cluster as the acoustic/communicative face of כָּבוֹד.

merge_notes.reason: The heart (לֵּב) is a bechina of the soul (נֶפֶשׁ) — 'אֵלֶיךָ ה׳ נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא, פֵּרוּשׁ רַשִׁ׳׳י: לִבִּי אֲכַוֵּן'. In Torah #67 the central drama is that the נֶפֶשׁ is rooted in כָּבוֹד (kavod is the mother and root of all souls), and the neglect of heartfelt prayer (כַּוָּנַת הַלֵּב) causes the נֶפֶשׁ to distance itself from its root, the כָּבוֹד. The nefesh/lev pair participates in the same essential domain as כָּבוֹד: the inner life of the human being whose source and home is the divine honor.

Thunder is explicitly the voice of כָּבוֹד — 'אֵל הַכָּבוֹד הִרְעִים ה׳ עַל מַיִם רַבִּים' (Psalm 29:3). Good tidings (שְׁמוּעָה טוֹבָה) = the sound of thunder that heals the weary soul. The Torah #67 text (section 8) explicitly states: 'שְׁמוּעָה טוֹבָה זֶה בְחִינַת קוֹל הָרְעָמִים... שֶׁמְּתַקְּנִין הִתְרַחֲקוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ מִן הַכָּבוֹד'. The sound-pair is a face of the divine honor domain.

packages.label: אַהֲבָה וְאַבְרָהָם
packages.reason: Three-node component: אַבְרָהָם, אַהֲבָה, and יַד יָמִין are all bechina of each other. Abraham is the bechina of love (אַהֲבָה), which is the bechina of the right hand (יַד יָמִין). These three share a single essential nature: the quality of חֶסֶד — outpouring, expansive, nurturing love — as the power that grows and raises the new soul after birth. In Torah #67 section 7, after the soul is born through fear (יִרְאָה), it is raised and grown through love — 'מְגַדְּלִין אוֹתָהּ עַל־יְדֵי הָאַהֲבָה, בְּחִינַת אַבְרָהָם... בְּחִינַת יַד יָמִין.' All three are the same essential force — chesed/ahavah — viewed from different angles (patriarchal archetype, emotional quality, physical metaphor of the outstretched right hand). Merged from raw component C2 which already has 3 nodes; no additional merges needed.

packages.label: צְדָקָה וְחֶסֶד
packages.reason: Three-node component: צְדָקָה (charity/righteousness), חֲמִשָּׁה חֲסָדִים (five acts of lovingkindness), and חֶסֶד (lovingkindness). The Torah #67 text (section 5) states explicitly: 'צְדָקָה הִיא בְחִינַת חֲמִשָּׁה חֲסָדִים, כִּי הַצְּדָקָה הִיא בְחִינַת חֶסֶד.' These three concepts share the essential nature of generous, outflowing divine grace that rescues the holy kingdom from the fallen state. Charity is the operative instrument by which the letter ה is added to צֶדֶק (justice) to form צְדָקָה — meaning the five hasadim (corresponding to the ה = five) transform bare justice into redemptive giving. This cluster is the 'rescue force' that lifts the Malkhut from exile. Note the relationship of this package to Package 2 (Love/Abraham): the two are distinct at the level of bechina — Package 2 captures the essential nature of love as the raising/nurturing force (right hand, Abraham, growth), while Package 3 captures charity as the specific redemptive instrument of the five hasadim that elevates the fallen kingdom from the sitra achra. They are parallel aspects of the chesed domain but each is a distinct essential nature in this Torah's argument.

packages.label: עַזֵּי פָּנִים וּמַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה
packages.label_en: The Brazen-Faced and the Evil Kingdom
packages.reason: Core component: עַזֵּי פָּנִים (the insolent/brazen-faced) ↔ כְּלָבִים עַזֵּי נֶפֶשׁ (the dogs with brazen souls). These two are bechina of each other, both expressing the essential nature of impudent leadership that seizes honor when the holy Malkhut falls. In Torah #67 section 3, the Rebbe teaches: the fallen person who lacks kavod is like 'מַלְכוּתָא בְּלָא תָגָא' (a kingdom without a crown). The brazen-faced are the human embodiment of the evil kingdom that fills the vacuum when the table-of-holiness fails. They are also called by the verse 'פְּנֵי הַדּוֹר כִּפְנֵי הַכֶּלֶב' (the face of the generation is like the face of a dog, Sota 49b). Two small 2-node components are merged here: (a) שִׁכְחָה↔עֲנָנִין דִּמְכַסְּיָן עַל עֵינִין — forgetting/clouds-covering-the-eyes is the mechanism by which the wisdom of sages is hidden, which is what gives the brazen ones their power; the essential nature is 'the darkness that hides the holy light' and belongs in the evil domain alongside the brazen ones; (b) מוֹתָרוֹת שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ↔בִּינָה יְתֵרָה — the surplus brain matter from which the enemies suckle belongs in the evil domain because it is the material from which the שְׂעָרוֹת (hairs) grow, and those hairs are the channels through which enemies and adversaries draw their nourishment (Torah #67 section 6: 'מֵהֶם יוֹנְקִים הָאוֹיְבִים'). The essential nature of the excess-brain/binah-yeteira pair is 'the nutriment of the adversaries' — squarely in the evil domain as the food of the opposing forces.

merge_notes.reason: Forgetting is the bechina of clouds-that-cover-the-eyes ('הַשִּׁכְחָה הוּא בְחִינַת עֲנָנִין דִּמְכַסְּיָן עַל עֵינִין'). When the elder forgets his learning, it is as if clouds have covered his inner sight. This is the mechanism by which holy wisdom disappears from the world, creating the void that the brazen ones exploit. The essential nature of both concepts is 'spiritual darkness / concealment of wisdom' — the evil-side condition that enables the brazen-faced to dominate. It belongs with the evil-domain cluster.

'מוֹתָרוֹת שֶׁבַּמֹּחַ' = the surplus/excess of the brain matter = the 'בִּינָה יְתֵרָה' given to woman (Nidda 45b, quoted at Torah #67's opening). The Torah explains that from these brain excesses grow the שְׂעָרוֹת (hairs), and from those hairs the enemies (אוֹיְבִים, שׂוֹנְאִים) suckle their nourishment. This pair is therefore the root nutriment of the adversarial forces — it is an evil-domain concept in this Torah, not a neutral or positive one. It belongs alongside the brazen-ones and the forgetting/concealment cluster as part of the domain of 'forces that feed on holiness when it is mismanaged.'

packages.label: יִלֵּד וְגִדּוּל הַנֶּפֶשׁ
packages.reason: Three-node component: קִשּׁוּי לֵילֵד (difficulty in childbirth), גִּדּוּל הַנֶּפֶשׁ (raising/growing the soul), and 'צָרָה כְּמַבְכִּירָה' (anguish like a woman in first labor). These three share the essential domain of the birth-pain / growth-pain nexus. In Torah #67 section 7, the Rebbe states: 'קִשּׁוּי לֵילֵד, וְגַם הוּא בְחִינַת גִּדּוּל הַנֶּפֶשׁ, בְּחִינַת (זְכַרְיָה י׳׳ב): ׳כְּהָמִיר עַל הַבְּכוֹר׳, שֶׁהוּא צַעַר הַגִּדּוּל.' And 'צָרָה כְּמַבְכִּירָה' = the bechina of birth-difficulty. These three are all the same essential reality: the pain of bringing a new soul into the world and raising it. The polarity is neutral because the birth-pain is a structural feature of the spiritual process — it is not inherently evil (it is the resistance the soul meets when entering the world) nor is it simply 'good' (it is a form of suffering). It is the neutral force of the creative threshold — the birthpang that accompanies all significant spiritual emergence.
